messages.content: Who is the best singer in Jazz

message.content:
When it comes to jazz vocalists, “best” is always a matter of taste and context, but a few names consistently rise to the top of most lists:

| Singer | Why they’re often called the best |
|--------|-----------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable diction, scat‑sing ability, and pure tone set a standard for jazz singing. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her emotive phrasing and unique vocal timbre made songs like “Strange Fruit” and “God Bless the Child” unforgettable. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (vocalist) | Though famous as a trumpeter, his gravelly voice and charismatic delivery on tracks such as “What a Wonderful World” made him a jazz icon. |
| **Frank Sinatra** | His smooth phrasing and swing feel turned standards into timeless classics. |
| **Nat King Cole** | A blend of jazz, pop, and blues, his warm baritone and storytelling style earned him the nickname “The King of Swing.” |

If you’re looking for a single name, **Ella Fitzgerald** is often cited as the definitive benchmark for jazz singing because of her technical mastery, emotional depth, and lasting influence on generations of vocalists.
